intro.text: Agents are ones you make: each is someone you talk to, with optional work it does on its own. deploy.local runs your apps and coding agents on computers you own. Every screen loads the deploy.local design system.

desktop.text: Desktop app: Electron on Mac, Linux and Windows; iOS stays SwiftUI. The window loads deploy.local from your coordinator, trusting only its CA. The shell adds the menu bar or tray, notifications, a login item, the bundled worker (installing the app adds a computer) and the native control helper for screen use. It notifies only for Waiting on you items and failing apps.

cli.text: CLI proposal. Today bin/deploy.js is one 3,389-line file with 36 command lines and 25 global options. Proposed: six groups in the app's words, [app] as an optional positional, steps instead of log dumps, the dark theme's palette, --json everywhere and exit code 3 while something waits on you. Old commands keep working for one release.

build.text: Build rules for v2: the server sends each conversation as typed events (decision, work log, task link, answer, report) and every client renders them, folding but never dropping a decision. Tabs appear only once their thing exists. Words are taught once, where they first happen. Agents answer when you talk to them. Optional background work reports briefly when it finishes or needs a decision.

mac-chrome-how.text:
Proposal. Electron titleBarStyle hiddenInset: the traffic lights live in the first 92 px of the 52 px top row.

• Expanded: the 256 px sidebar shows only the d mark beside the lights, then Search and Collapse. Each control keeps a 32 px target; the brand name remains accessible. Full screen restores the wordmark and removes the light gutter.
• Collapsed: one 64 px rail, also at 700 px. Its items start below the 52 px top row. The lights extend into reserved space beside it; the main header starts 44 px inside the main pane (108 px from the window edge). No mark or title sits under the lights.
• One device preference across Projects, a task’s Changes, a project’s Code and Design. New devices start expanded. Page changes and resizing never change that preference. The expanded sidebar stays 256 px at 700; secondary content folds instead.
• Drag empty top-row space; buttons, links and fields remain clickable. Double-click follows the Mac zoom setting. Design panels fold independently and never hide the app sidebar.
• These boards show both saved choices. Native lights and their reserved space exist only in the Mac app.

welcome-narrow-note.text: For approval. In the browser, below 820px the welcome sidebar hides and the menu button opens it. In the Mac app, follow the Mac chrome boards instead: the saved expanded sidebar or rail stays on the left at 700px, with a dedicated top-row reserve for the traffic lights.

design-canvas-how.text:
How it works. Designs live in the repo, so any agent (Codex, Claude) or a person can change them on a branch:
• design/canvas.json: sections, board positions, notes
• design/boards/<Name>.html: one self-contained board, styled by the shipped design-system CSS
• design/notes/<Name>.md: what the board is for and the decisions behind it
A visual change is a design change on a branch. Its task gets a Design tab with Before (main) and After (this branch). Approving merges design/ into main, which makes the After the design; then the build task starts. deploy.local renders all of it; no claude.ai needed.

design-canvas-changes.text:
Design: how it works
• Designs live in the repo in design/: canvas.json plus one HTML file per board, built from the design system. Every element has a stable layer ID (data-layer).
• Layout follows Figma: navigation on the left (the d menu with Waiting on you, Designs and the branch, File | Assets, Pages = sections, Layers), the full properties panel on the right, the tool bar at the bottom with vector tools.
• Edits save to a design branch; main changes only through Propose for review and approval (Design tab, chat card, Waiting on you).
• Agents edit through design tools (read, render, structured edits, presence, comments, propose), each on its own branch, shown as a live overlay you accept or discard.
• iPad uses the desktop layout; iPhone has the full canvas with Layers and Edit as sheets.

Build order:
1. Canvas, Layers, Comments, review, and Ask an agent with live editing.
2. Direct edits: text, properties and tokens.
3. Vector tools and Assets.

design-review-notes-how.text:
Reviewing changes that are not boards
• Opening a design item in Waiting on you shows its review, task or not: changed boards as Before and After, and changed canvas notes as their text, Before and After, with the new lines marked.
• The list on the left names each change: a board by its name, a note by its first line, tagged Note.
• The item's line says what changed in words: “The note “Drawing: how it works” changed on design/drawing-note”, or “2 boards and 1 note changed”; never “1 design files”.
• iPhone shows the same: the note's text in place of a board, with Before and After.

design-prototype-how.text:
Prototype and Play: how boards connect
• Links already live in the boards: a layer that opens another board carries its link (href). 143 of 171 boards have them.
• Prototype, beside Edit and Comments, draws the selected board's links on the canvas: a line from each layer to the board it opens, the selected layer's line strongest. The repeated sidebar links stay hidden until you show them.
• To see every connection while you move around the canvas, in any tab, turn on Connections in the tool bar (⇧C); see the Connections board.
• With a layer selected, Interaction says what a click does: On click › Go to a board. Change the board, remove the link, or drag the dot at the layer's edge onto a board. Saving writes the layer's link on your design branch, like any edit.
• The board section lists where the board leads and what leads to it; Flow says where Play starts (the page's first board unless you choose another).
• Play (▷, top right) opens the start board full screen and follows links: Back, the trail of boards you passed through, Restart, and the width (1440, 700, 390). Clicking where there's no link lights up the links. Esc or Exit returns to the canvas.
• On iPad, Play is tap to follow, swipe from the left edge to go back, Done to leave.

design-draw-how.text:
Drawing: how it works
• Rectangle, Ellipse and Line (the shape menu, or R, O, L) draw inside a board where you drag. The shape keeps that spot (X and Y) and size, filled surface with a line stroke, and saves to the board on your design branch.
• Text (T): click inside a board to place a text layer and type; Enter keeps it.
• Pen (P): a stroke with Apple Pencil, or a drag, inks a mark on the canvas: danger, W 2.5, the same width on screen at any zoom. Marks sit beside boards like sticky notes, never inside one, and save to canvas.json. Select one to set its rotation, size, opacity, stroke colour, W and Arrow end; drag it to move it; Delete removes it. Tapping points instead draws a vector in a board; Enter, or a tap on the first point, ends it.
• Frame (F): drag on empty canvas to make a new board (Web 1440 or Phone 390 by its width, named Board N until you rename it); inside a board it makes a frame layer.
• Sticky notes (S): click on the canvas; they save to canvas.json and show over the boards they point at. Layers lists a page's marks and sticky notes after its boards.
• Escape goes back to Move (V); the pen keeps inking until you do. Layers drawn in a board can be edited in the properties panel and undone with Reset.

design-native-how.text:
Design on iPhone and iPad
• Projects › a project › Design opens the Design page full screen, signed in as you. ‹ goes back to the project.
• iPad shows the desktop layout (the iPad board) and draws with Apple Pencil through the pen tool; iPhone shows the phone layout (these boards).
• Approving from Waiting on you and the design card in a task's chat stay native and show rendered boards.
• Ask has no agent choice: a design ask runs as its own task, on any free computer or the one you pick.

projects-live-link.text:
For approval. Every running app says where it comes from.
• Live: each row names its project (or From Discover, or No project).
• An app opens as Live › app, with Project, Repository, Release and Computer as links: app → project → repository → release.
• A project’s Overview lists what is Running: each app with health, address and computer, opening its page on Live.

projects-5.text:
Code and pull requests
Web app
iPhone: later

Code reads like GitHub and Gitea: files, then the README. Every pull request opens; one no task opened shows read-only, with its commits and files.

projects-rail-how.text:
One sidebar choice, remembered everywhere on this device
• New devices start with the full 256 px sidebar. Collapse selects the 64 px rail on Projects, Changes, Code and Design alike. There are no page-kind defaults or separate memories.
• Collapse sits beside Search; Expand sits above the account in the rail. ⌘\ toggles the same preference everywhere. Page changes and resizing preserve it; both states fit at 700 px.
• The rail keeps New task, Projects, Live, Computers, Design, Waiting on you and Settings on the left. Hover or keyboard focus names each icon. Agents and Today remain in the full sidebar, one Expand or ⌘K away.
• MacChromeNarrow shows the temporary expanded sidebar after pressing the rail’s download icon. Closing update details restores the saved 64 px rail; this temporary expansion never writes the sidebar preference. A 52 px top strip reserves room for native lights; full screen removes that strip and its gutter.
• DesignMac and DesignConnections show an owner who chose the rail. Hiding Design panels affects only those panels, never the app navigation.

design-connections-how.text:
Connections: see how boards link without opening Prototype
• Connections, the last button in the tool bar (⇧C, also in the zoom menu), draws every link between boards on the page as an arrow, in Edit, Prototype and Comments alike. It stays on until you turn it off, per person.
• Arrows run board to board, one per pair, however many layers make that link. They're grey and thin so the boards stay readable.
• Select a board and its arrows turn violet: the boards it leads to and the boards that lead to it. Selecting a layer lights only that layer's link.
• Links to boards on other pages don't draw; the board's Connections section lists them under their page. Clicking a row goes to that board.
• Repeated links, like the sidebar on every board, stay hidden; the eye on the Sidebar row draws them too.
• Narrow windows show the same arrows; the Connections section sits in the bottom sheet.

self-update.text: SER is released like any other app, by pushing to its repository. Its update status and recovery pages remain under Computers → deploy.local updates. There is no SER update entry in the sidebar, for administrators or anyone else. The former sidebar status layers now live within those pages. Preparing and activating a SER release still verifies the build, backs up the databases and restores the previous release if health checks fail. Mac app updates are separate and appear only inside the Mac app.

mac-app-update.text:
deploy.local for Mac updates
• Check GET /desktop/version on the coordinator this Mac app is connected to, on launch and every 4 hours. Use its version and short commit, and the darwin-arm64 target’s file, size and sha256. The commit and byte counts on these boards are example data.
• Only the Mac app shows the one-line, nav-height update row, immediately above the account. Details and actions live INSIDE the expanded 256 px sidebar: a popover 8 px directly above the compact row, filling its inner width (about 240 px) with the same 8 px side insets as nav items. Use the design system menu surface, border and shadow; clip the shadow at the sidebar edge so nothing crosses onto the page. At 1440 and 700 px it overlays the lower task list without moving rows, changing list height or changing its scroll position. All update boards include a full task list; actions stack to fit the narrow surface. Pressing the row opens the popover; Escape or an outside click closes it while the download keeps going. It never appears in a browser and never describes SER updating itself. No row when the app is current; a failed background check must not claim it is current.
• Update available opens the popover; Download update starts downloading the published /desktop/ zip. Progress uses actual bytes and total size; Cancel stops and discards the partial download, leaving the installed app unchanged. Downloading 42% rounds 54 of 130 MB.
• After download, show Checking download… in the popover with no actions; the compact row or rail icon shows progress. MacChromeNarrow draws this checking state. Check SHA-256 against the published value before anything changes; only then offer Restart to update. A mismatch leaves the old app untouched and offers Try again. Network errors use “The download stopped. Nothing was changed.” with Try again.
• Restart to update is one press: remember the current page, keep the popover open with a spinner and “Installing… Reopening this page in a moment.” briefly, quit, replace the app in place and reopen on the same coordinator and page. Keep the old app until the new one opens successfully; restore it if installation or launch fails. Do not silently discard the previous app.
• The collapsed rail keeps one download icon above the account, with a small progress or failure glyph and a named tooltip. Pressing it temporarily expands the sidebar to 256 px and opens the same in-sidebar popover, without starting Download or Restart. This expansion never changes the remembered sidebar choice. MacChromeNarrow draws the temporary expanded checking state; DesignMac shows the closed failed icon and follows the same behavior. Escape, an outside click, pressing the update row again, Collapse, Later or the quiet Dismiss action close details; if opened from the rail, collapse back to 64 px and return focus to the download icon. A download or check continues and its icon remains available to reopen details. If opened from an already expanded sidebar, closing details leaves it expanded. Preserve the task list’s scroll position throughout; resizing or changing update state while details are open does not save an expanded preference.
• The install handoff and restoring the same page require implementation verification after this design is approved; these are static review boards.

design-review-compare.text: Compare with a slider (default) or onion skin. New boards say New board and have nothing to compare; removed boards show Before. The choice is remembered.

design-review-compare-interaction.text:
Comparison behavior for implementation after approval
• Align Before and After at the same origin, viewport width and scale. Slider shows Before left of the divider and After right. The web board draws a drag at 60% After; the phone review draws 50% After.
• Drag the 44 px handle with one finger on iPhone or the pointer on web. Keep the drag captured until release; a swipe outside the handle scrolls the review. Arrow keys and VoiceOver adjustments move the handle in 1% steps; Home/End reach the edges. Expose an adjustable slider named Compare, with value text such as “50% After”. Moving left reveals more After.
• Onion skin places After over opaque Before at the same size. The chat board draws 40% After. The opacity control below the image runs from 0% Before to 100% After, with the same keyboard and VoiceOver support.
• Start in Slider. Remember the person’s Slider / Onion skin choice across review, chat and boards on this device; do not reset it when switching boards.
• New boards show only After with a New board tag, and no compare controls. Removed boards show only Before with a Removed tag, and no compare controls. Neither changes the saved mode.
• Text-only and note-only changes retain the existing line-by-line note review (DesignReviewNote and DesignReviewNotePhone); no image comparison controls.
• These are static design drawings; gestures and saved preferences are specified here, not implemented in these boards.

decision-content.text: A decision shows what it is about: an agent's question shows the reply it refers to (the agent's latest message in the task), a merge shows its diff, a release what ships. Names, never IDs. Nothing that looks pressable is inert: no sample suggestions, no empty-state cards that repeat the composer. An empty Today has no section header. Waiting rows show the agent’s name and reply preview, never its ID.

question-decision-behavior.text: QuestionDecision / QuestionDecisionPhone: the draft is the agent's latest reply in this decision's task, rendered as markdown above every answer action. Scroll the bordered preview to read the full supplied reply; Open the task opens that task's whole conversation. Show “Scroll to read more” only when the content is taller than its block: omit it on the web board where everything fits, keeping Open the task right-aligned, and keep it on the phone board where the content overflows. A design decision shows its boards. Empty and whitespace-only answers keep Answer disabled; entering text enables it. Web: 1440 and 700 px. iPhone sheet: 390 px. Asked 12m ago is an example relative time.

new-agent-phone.text:
New agent is a name and an avatar; you teach it in the chat; details and routines live behind its name.
• + in the web sidebar or the iPhone Agents header opens NewAgentBlank / NewAgentBlankPhone; NewAgent / NewAgentPhone show a filled name after an avatar choice. Only avatar, Shuffle, color, Name and Create. No templates, generated draft, purpose, access, approvals or schedule in creation. Blank or whitespace-only names disable Create; trim on save. Creation failures keep the entered name and chosen avatar for retry.
• Create opens AgentHello / AgentHelloPhone: a big avatar, name, “Tell <name> what you want it to do. It remembers.” and four suggested first messages. Tapping a suggestion fills the composer for editing; it sends only when you press Send. No invented greeting, task, routine or history. All five action rules initially Ask.
• The name/avatar in the chat header opens AgentSettings / AgentInfoPhone. Edit the avatar, color and name; What it does reflects what it learned from your messages and can be edited. Save keeps these changes; closing without Save preserves the saved version. Phone editing is supported here, not deferred to a computer.
• Routines are optional and initially empty: “No routines yet”, “Runs on its own” and Add a routine. AgentRoutine / AgentRoutinePhone draw that action: When to run and What to do. Adding a routine never runs it immediately. Existing routines use the same editor with their saved values and Save routine / Delete routine actions. History and Run now live in AgentRuns / AgentRunsPhone. The later chat/details fixtures show one confirmed Friday routine and Start a task Allowed, set after creation.
• Phone sheets scroll between the pinned header and action, resize above the keyboard, keep the focused field visible and respect safe areas. Touch targets are at least 44 px. The ten color choices wrap into two rows of five on iPhone; on web they form one row. The owner will render 1440/700/390 and commit; this branch contains design only.

settings-phone-behavior.text:
iPhone Settings · nothing that looks pressable is inert
• Account is identity, with no link or chevron.
• Notification settings and Paired devices are full-width rows with chevrons. They open the existing V2NotificationSettings and V2DevicesView sheets; these static boards specify those native destinations with data-destination.
• What agents may do opens SettingsApprovalsPhone. Done dismisses it back to Settings. Each agent’s rules are plain, read-only action/value rows: Ask, Allowed or Never. No editable chips, switches or chevrons. Change these in Settings on a computer.
• SettingsAgents and SettingsApprovalsPhone show all five saved agents. Release notes writer: Start a task Allowed, the other four actions Ask. Ops watcher, Code reviewer, Researcher and Designer: all five actions Ask in the shared settings snapshot. The agent list comes from the coordinator; no built-ins. Creation defaults every action to Ask without an approvals step. This Settings sheet remains read-only, with changes made on a computer. When opened from agent details, Done returns to those details; from Settings, it returns to Settings.
• Backups opens the existing restore sheet (RestorePhone); its copy stays “Restore to a copy”.
• Appearance opens a menu: System (selected), Light, Dark. Choosing a value immediately applies and remembers this iPhone’s appearance preference; System follows iOS.
• Screen use, removing data and secrets stay on a computer. This is a plain footnote under the groups.
• The settings list scrolls above a full-width, centered destructive Sign out button at the bottom. Sign out uses the existing sign-out flow. No app implementation changes in this design pass.
• Team limits is a separate editable section on iPhone. Existing per-action permission rows remain read-only. Archive is immutable Always asks, outside the five action selectors.

chat-agents-model.text:
Agents are conversations first — approved direction; additions for review
• New agent is a name and an avatar; you teach it in the chat; details and routines live behind its name. No built-in agents and no templates. The fixture has five saved agents: Release notes writer (variant28, af61f2), Ops watcher (variant21, 2fb5a3), Code reviewer (variant29, 76a7ff), Researcher (variant10, ffaa64), Designer (variant03, e66bb8); the 35 picker glyphs are avatar choices, not saved agents.
• Avatars are DiceBear Glyphs (@dicebear/core 10 + @dicebear/styles, bundled, drawn offline): one of 35 glyphs plus one color, never a random photo. One color draws the whole avatar: a tinted circle, the glyph and darker shoulders. An agent stores its glyph and color; a new agent starts with a random glyph and color picked when the dialog opens (blank fixture: variant07, ff4d6f). Typing a name never changes its glyph; Shuffle and Choose avatar do. Glyphs is CC BY 4.0 by Matt Houser (a remix of “Abstract Avatars for All Creative Profile Use”): credit him in Settings → General (Credits at the bottom).
• AvatarPicker boards show the state reached by tapping the large avatar in creation or details. All 35 glyphs show in the current color, the chosen one outlined. The current example is Release notes writer as glyph 28 in Violet everywhere: list, chat, task mention and approvals. Selection keeps the current color; a swatch keeps the current drawing; Shuffle picks a glyph/color pair. Done returns to the invoking surface, preserving the Name and all other edits. Cancel restores the prior avatar. The picker is shared by creation and details, not another creation step.
• Ten colors: Violet #af61f2, Blue #76a7ff, Green #75c675, Amber #e8b130, Red #ff4d6f, Indigo #525fa3, Teal #2fb5a3, Orange #ffaa64, Pink #e66bb8, Gray #8c8c8c (Glyphs' own palette plus four). These are identity colors, never status indicators; status keeps its own icon and label.
• Open an agent to its conversation. Ordinary answers stay prose. Requested work appears as an attributed linked task. Sidebar and Work rows show avatar, name, last message and time. An empty conversation says Say hello with no fabricated timestamp. No agents keeps the + and the invitation to make one. The web sidebar folds below 820 px; chat, details and dialogs remain usable at 700 px.
• Details contain avatar/color, Name, editable What it does, Routines (“Runs on its own”), What it may use (project and computers), and an approvals summary with a link. What it does updates from explicit instructions in chat; it is not a generated pre-creation draft. New agents begin with no learned purpose and no routines. No per-agent connected-app setup: connections belong to the account and are managed in account settings. Project and computer access still applies to each agent.
• TaskMention / TaskMentionPhone keep @ in the composer: only saved agents are offered, filtered by name. Select inserts a stable @Name reference; sending delivers it. Arrow keys, Enter and Escape work on web. No match says No matching agents; no agents offers New agent. The picker stays above the keyboard. Mentions do not expand resource access or bypass approvals.
• Agents may message other saved agents: use the same identity and attributed-message model, surface the sender and recipient, keep their replies in the originating conversation, and apply each agent’s own access and approval rules. no autonomous message loops or automatic routines implied by a mention.
• Routines are separate saved work with their own When to run and What to do, not a single switch on the agent’s learned purpose. The proposed weekly fixture is Fridays at 16:00 on SER’s clock. AgentTaught and agent details show it pending; AgentRoutine shows review before confirmation. AgentPage and AgentRuns show the later saved routine and its history, after confirmation and subsequent Fridays. 16:00 is the agent’s suggestion, not a time supplied by the owner. Absent history never reads as a successful run. Routine prompts, multiple routines, weekly recurrence, avatar persistence, learning from messages and agent-to-agent routing require implementation after approval; existing APIs are not assumed to already support this proposal. The weekly choice reveals a weekday before saving.
• The current chat/task bridge still needs approval-aware task creation, structured mention recipients and enforced resource scope. Retain the five Ask / Allowed / Never actions and the connected model/default. Saved legacy apps/trigger values must survive an eventual migration; removing their controls is not permission to erase them. No implementation, merge, push or release is part of this branch.
• Instructions in chat update What it does with a visible, attributed “Saved to What it does · Edit” receipt. Time-based requests propose a routine you confirm; they never silently save a routine. AgentTaught / AgentTaughtPhone show this moment.
• NewAgentBlank / NewAgentBlankPhone are the immediate + state: empty Name with placeholder, visibly disabled Create (aria-disabled). NewAgent / NewAgentPhone remain filled examples after choosing the violet glyph. Name-only edits preserve the random avatar. Picker Done returns to its invoking state and keeps the name.
• Saved-agent list links carry the selected agent identity; query examples reuse the chat layout with that agent’s name, glyph, color and history. The drawn chat and details fixtures remain Release notes writer. Ops incident/report and Release notes writer long-history boards are examples of owner-created agents with access and confirmed routines, never built-ins. The five-agent list previews represent the shared current snapshot, independent of historical or creation-state examples.
• Confirm routine saves a schedule with no runs yet (AgentRuns?state=scheduled). Its initial history is “No runs yet · Next Friday at 16:00”; Run now is a separate explicit action. The drawn AgentRuns fixture is a later historical state. No routine begins immediately on confirmation.
• A taught beat is separate from a routine: it may inspect accessible projects in its stage scope and bring proposals. Nothing changes without owner approval. Time-based work still requires a confirmed routine. Looks after is editable behind the agent name; see the adjacent care flow. Designer’s shared last message is “Proposed a calmer Tally header.” · Tue.

project-care-model.text:
Your agents look after your projects
• Flow below reads left to right, then down: beat → noticing → proposal → approve → task/design review → weekly summary → archive → limits. Projects and Care, existing Waiting on you, Home/Work and Settings are sufficient; no new navigation item.
• Only the owner changes stage. Active accepts Fix, Update, Improvement, Feature idea, Design and Archive. Maintained accepts Fix and Update only; feature/design beats stop there. Done accepts nothing, including health checks. Ops watches running apps subject to stage/access; it may propose archiving an idle Active project, never infer Done or archive it. Manual archive is available for Active and Maintained. Moving to Maintained withdraws incompatible proposals and pauses previously approved incompatible work for the owner to review.
• Saved agents are owner-created, not built-ins. Code reviewer: quality and dependency updates across accessible Active and Maintained. Researcher: feature ideas across Active. Designer: design polish across Active (variant03/e66bb8, Tue preview). Ops watcher: health of running apps and archive suggestions for idle Active projects. Release notes writer keeps its separate confirmed routine. Looks after supports all Active, all Active and Maintained, or chosen projects, intersected with granted access and stage defaults. Teaching saves a visible editable receipt; it grants no resource access. The earlier beat receipt excludes recipes because Code reviewer lacks access. New agents have no beat until taught. Unassigned and Quiet boards are independent states, not simultaneous.
• Beats can perform read-only checks and propose; routines still require explicit confirmation. A proposal includes an agent, project, kind, evidence revision/source, proposed work and rough size. Approve grants only that scoped task; Never blocks it, Ask is satisfied by this explicit scope only, Allowed never skips proposal approval. Recheck stage, evidence, access, permissions and limits atomically at answer time and again before execution. A changed evidence revision withdraws it as “This no longer applies”, removes it from Waiting, frees its slot and preserves the record in Answered. No stale Approve. No duplicate task when two devices answer.
• Not now closes the item, frees the slot and suppresses the same finding until evidence materially changes; Reopen is in Answered. Stop suggesting this stores an agent + project + finding-family preference, not a global kind ban; management and Undo live in Looks after. Archive suppression is separate. Changed evidence does not bypass that explicit suppression.
• Approval never merges, ships, releases or changes stage itself. Code goes through PRs and the existing five Ask/Allowed/Never rules. Every visible change, including a Feature or Fix with UI effects, goes through design branch → Before/After owner review → approved design on main → implementation. ProposalDesign’s small drawing is an illustrative direction, not an approved board. CareDesignReview is the subsequent review state; requests for changes return to that design conversation and require review again. Existing DesignReview comparison behavior applies at 1440/700 and 390 on phone. Archive always asks and cannot be Allowed. Existing incident permissions remain separate; a care beat cannot use them as a bypass.
• Team limits are per owner: maximum 5 open care proposals across all agents/projects; maximum 3 team-opened PRs per project per calendar week, including closed PRs. Reserve budgets atomically to prevent races. Other decisions do not consume proposal slots. The five current proposals: home-gym Fix, tally Feature, tally Design, immich Update, recipes Archive. Improvement, stale, after-answer and stage-change boards are separate snapshots, not extra open proposals. At cap, agents wait and coalesce findings; recheck them before presenting later. Approved code work queues before creating a branch/PR when budget is exhausted. Design-only review can continue; build waits. Weekly PR budget resets Monday 00:00 in the owner timezone; restarting an agent never resets it.
• Quiet hours 22:00–08:00 America/New_York: no care checks, new care tasks or proposal notifications; already approved running work can finish. Urgent app incident handling stays under existing explicit rules. Local wall-clock boundaries handle DST. Owner can change the limits and hours on web or phone. Defaults by stage are shown plainly and cannot widen Done beyond nothing or Maintained beyond Fix/Update in this version.
• Archive preview lists every affected app. Revalidate active tasks/PRs before executing; pause conflicting work and require the owner to resolve it. Stop apps, take a named final backup of repository/app data/configuration, verify it, make the repository read-only, then atomically move to Done, remove from sidebar/active lists, close proposals and stop beats/routines for that project. Retain backup indefinitely until explicit deletion; no hidden 30-day expiry. Failure keeps original stage/data and shows actual app state; retry resumes safely. Manual archive uses the same preview, with actual project-specific evidence; no silent stage dropdown archive.
• Done is available only under Projects → Done. Restore is one explicit action: verify retained backup, bring back writable repository and app configuration/data, move to Maintained and restore applicable access-scoped Fix/Update beats. Apps remain stopped until the owner starts them. Do not reopen old proposals, resume old tasks or start routines automatically. Failure leaves Done and the retained backup intact. kettle-timer is an independent historical Done example, not an invented completion of the recipes archive.
• Monday 09:00 owner-local time produces exactly one Home/Work message from recorded events, grouped by project: done, proposed, needs you. Link each claim to its actual source; no event means no success claim. WeeklySummary is a historical message; a line about last week’s PR cap describes that time, not the current reset. Counts in current Care reflect its own week. CareActivity supplies the illustrative source records; implementation must read actual check, task, PR, design, answer and archive events. Unavailable signals say Unavailable, never healthy/zero. Immich version/security numbers are brief-supplied design fixtures; exact upstream advisories, compatibility and backup plan remain required before an update can run.
• Server work required after design approval: persist stage/archive state and verified retained backups; typed beats and access intersections; read-only scheduled checks with evidence provenance; deduplicated proposal lifecycle and suppression preferences; transactional owner/project budgets and timezone scheduling; approval-aware task creation with idempotent answers; design-to-build linkage; PR/incident permission enforcement; safe resumable archive/restore with locks; shared event-backed Care and weekly summary APIs. Web, Mac and iPhone render the same events. No server support is assumed, and no app implementation is included.
• All fixtures are design examples, not claims about deployed projects. Boards scroll vertically where needed; five agent rows fit the web sidebar at 900 px and iPhone Work before lower history. The owner’s orchestrator renders 1440/700/390, regenerates glyph SVGs, reviews visual parity and commits. This edit does not render, commit, push, merge or release.
• Query links such as ?agent=designer and ?project=home-gym use the shared details/Care layout with that identity, stage, beats and evidence. Answer routes retain the originating proposal identity and render its exact agent/project/finding in the receipt; static generic answer boards show the shared layout. Manual archive reuses the same archive task with its selected project (ArchiveManualProgress draws tally). No cross-project navigation may silently change the target.
